ruling: Subdivisions and Partitions. Both mentions sit in the sentence after the one this screen reads: "There is no minimum lot size or dimension for development of land or creation of new lots in commercial zones. Creation of new lots is subject to the regulations of Section 450." Same split as Portland 33.613 — the development half is the test an existing lot has to pass, and the creation half is a plat that produces the lot in the first place. Parked rather than closed: no pod in flats/config/pods declares plat: unit_lots, so this screen never creates a lot. The day one does, this is a fetch.

ruling: "Subdivisions, Partitions, Replats, Middle Housing Land Divisions." Both mentions are ZDO Table 1012 footnotes permitting a middle housing land division as an exception to a lot standard, and the parent-lot standards this layer already encodes are the ones that govern while the pod sits on one lot. Parked rather than closed: no pod in flats/config/pods declares plat: unit_lots, so this screen never creates a lot. The day one does, this is a fetch.

ruling: LOC 50.06.001.5.b is cited as a Height Limitation "for non-single-family dwellings" in five of the dimensional table's cross-reference blocks, including the WLG and EC zones. The pod is a non-single-family dwelling and the encoded Lake Oswego heights leave two to four feet of slack over 26 ft, so a design-chapter qualifier on height is exactly the Gresham 7.0420 shape. Chapter 50.06 is not held.

sample: Creation of new lots is subject to the regulations of Chapter 33.613, Lots in Commercial/Mixed
ruling: Lots in Commercial/Mixed Use Zones. The sentence this screen reads -- "There is no required minimum lot size for development of land in commercial/mixed use zones" -- is followed by one sending lot *creation* to this chapter. Creating a lot is not a test an existing lot has to pass to be built on, and CR, CM1, CM2, CM3, CE and CX are encoded on the development half of that pair. The campus institutional zones state both halves outright, which is what shows the split is the code's and not a reading of it. Parked rather than closed: no pod in flats/config/pods declares plat: unit_lots, so this screen never creates a lot. The day one does, this is a fetch.

sample: Lot size regulations are in Chapters 33.614 and 33.615.
ruling: "Lot size regulations are in Chapters 33.614 and 33.615", the whole of what 33.140 says about lot size in the employment and industrial zones. Land-division chapters, same shape as 33.613 in the commercial chapter: how a lot may be created, not a minimum a built lot has to meet. EX is encoded exempt on that sentence. Parked with 33.613 for the same reason: no pod declares plat: unit_lots today.

ruling: Temporary Permits, cited by ZDO 315's one-dwelling-per-lot rule as an exception alongside Section 839, Accessory Dwelling Units. A temporary permit is not a path to a permanent four-unit building.

sample: 1 If a minimum lot size for the conditional use is established by Section 800, Special Use Requirements, it remains applicable.
ruling: Special Use Requirements, and it is a division heading rather than a section: the county serves one page per section and /planning/zdo800 is a 404. Its own citing sentence is gated on a use this pod is not -- "If a minimum lot size for the conditional use is established by Section 800, Special Use Requirements, it remains applicable" -- and Table 315-1 marks every Quadplexes cell P7,8, permitted rather than conditional. What the division contains is already here: note 8 sends this building to Section 845, which is stored, and 845 carries the one minimum lot size that governs the pod anywhere in unincorporated Clackamas.

sample: Accessory Dwelling Units, subject to Section 839
ruling: Accessory Dwelling Units, the section the ADU row of the use table points at: "Accessory Dwelling Units, subject to Section 839". A subordinate second unit on a lot with a house, and this screen places four attached primary ones. Its other mention is the same shape -- "Except as allowed by Section 839, Accessory Dwelling Units, or Section 1204, Temporary Permits, each lot of record may be developed with only one of the following" -- where 839 is named as an exception that ADDS a unit.

sample: 6 Dwellings not otherwise permitted in the applicable zoning district may nonetheless be permitted if they are developed as affordable housing, as defined in OR
ruling: Affordable Housing, and it points the opposite way from a standard: "Dwellings not otherwise permitted in the applicable zoning district may nonetheless be permitted if they are developed as affordable housing, as defined in ORS 197A.445(1), and subject to Section 846." Reading it could only admit lots this screen rejects on the use flag -- it cannot reject one it admits. That is the same reasoning applied to variances elsewhere in this corpus, and it holds a fortiori here because the permission is granted by statute rather than discretion.

sample: DWELLING: A building that contains one or more dwelling units. A dwelling may be a residential trailer or a manufactured dwelling but not a recreational vehicle
ruling: Recreational Vehicles as Second Dwellings: "P P P Recreational Vehicles as Second Dwellings, subject to Section 847", and "unless the vehicle is approved as a temporary dwelling pursuant to Section 1204, Temporary Permits, or as a second dwelling pursuant to Section 847". A vehicle, and a second one at that. Not four attached factory-built units on a foundation.

sample: (7) Mixed-use development within Gladstone Town Center. Commercial uses permitted in the mixed-use development include those listed as permitted in the C-2 zoni
ruling: The C-2 district''s permitted use list, reached from the mixed-use district: "Commercial uses permitted in the mixed-use development include those listed as permitted in the C-2 zoning district, GMC Section 17.18.020." It is cited to say which SHOPS may occupy the commercial half of a mixed-use building. The residential half is permitted by its own row, and this screen places a residential building on a lot of its own.

sample: “Residential planned unit development” means a residential (R) planned unit development as allowed under GMC Chapter 17.38 (Planned Unit Development) and is at
ruling: Planned Unit Development. Two of the three mentions open a zone's dimensional standards -- "Except as provided in GMC Chapters 17.38 (Planned Unit Development), 17.72 (Variances) and 17.76 (Exceptions), the following dimensional standards shall apply" -- so it stands in the same sentence as the setbacks and lot area this screen reads, which is why it ranked binding beside a minimum lot area. It is the exception clause, and every limb of it RELAXES: a PUD, a variance and an exception are three ways of being let off a standard. Reading it could admit lots this screen rejects and can never reject one it admits, which is `narrows_only` pointing the other way. 17.72 is already ruled here on that reasoning. The third mention settles it further: 17.06's definition of a residential PUD requires "at least 80,000 square feet in any zoning district", and anything smaller "must be approved by Planning Commission per GMC 17.38.020". A discretionary approval on a two-acre assembly is not a by-right screen.

sample: (A) A pedestrian circulation system plan consistent with GMC Section 17.50.020.
ruling: Pedestrian circulation, reached from 17.48.030(1)(i): a development with more than half an acre of new off-street surface parking must file a circulation plan, a tree canopy plan and a climate mitigation action. The pod's whole court is four stalls and their aisle, around two thousand square feet, so the threshold is an order of magnitude away from this building.

ruling: On-site traffic control sign standards, reached from 17.48.050(2)(c): a bicycle parking area not visible from the street needs a sign conforming to them. A specification for a sign, and the bicycle standards it hangs off are themselves refused in `defaults` for want of a field.

ruling: Clear Vision, reached from 17.48.040(1)(b): screening between a parking area and an abutting residential property "shall not conflict with GMC Chapter 17.54". A ceiling on how tall a hedge may be near a corner, which cannot take ground from a rear court -- the screen it qualifies is itself a fence or a hedge and this model gives it no width.

ruling: Setbacks for manufactured homes in a mobile home park. One sentence, printed once in each dimensional table and spanned by rowspan over every setback row, which is why it counts ten times. The pod is factory-built and is neither a manufactured dwelling nor sited on a rented space in a park, so the standard is about somebody else's building and 17.62 is not fetched.

sample: In an R-7.2 zoning district, the following uses and their accessory uses are allowed subject to GMC Chapter 17.70 (Conditional Uses):
ruling: Conditional Uses, and it is reached two ways rather than one. FOUR of the five mentions are the header of a zone's conditional list — "the following uses and their accessory uses are allowed subject to GMC Chapter 17.70" — and a fourplex is not on any of them. What is on the R-7.2 list is a "multi-household dwelling, five- to eight-unit building on a collector or minor arterial", beside churches, fire stations and nursing homes. Four units is one below the bottom of that range. That much has been true since this ruling was written and it stays true. The FIFTH mention arrived on 2026-09-03 with Chapter 17.28 and it is a different animal, so the old wording — "every mention is the header of a zone's conditional list" — was made false by a fetch and is corrected here rather than left to read as an absence claim. Recorded as a stated gap in Lot Analysis/quadfit/config/overlays.yaml beside the two Gladstone overlays that could be built. The ledger could not see that and was right not to: a "1012" in a Portland document is not this section, and resolving section numbers across jurisdictions would invent references rather than find them. The MAXIMUM density of 1012.05, applied to the VTH districts by 1012.06, is a density cap on middle housing and OAR 660-046-0220(2)(b) strikes it out -- the same preemption this corpus applies to every other maximum density it has read. sample: (3) Disabled Parking. Where required by this Code, Chapter 31 of the Uniform Building Code or the Americans With Disabilities Act, disabled parking spaces must
ruling: Chapter 31 of the Uniform Building Code, cited by WVDC 350.065(D)(3): "Where required by this Code, Chapter 31 of the Uniform Building Code or the Americans With Disabilities Act, disabled parking spaces must meet the dimension standards stated in Table 350-3." Both halves are now decided and neither requires anything of this building. The WVDC half supplies dimensions for a requirement stated somewhere else, and no row of Table 350-1A asks Household Living for an accessible space. The building-code half was parked from 2026-08 until 2026-09-03 and is now closed against the code itself. Oregon's current book is the 2025 Structural Specialty Code (IBC 2024 base, mandatory 2026-04-01), and its chain is explicit. OSSC 1106.3 requires accessible parking in Groups R-2, R-3 and R-4 only where the building is "required to have Accessible, Type A or Type B dwelling units." OSSC 1108.6.2.2.2 makes every unit of a four-or-more-unit structure a Type B unit, subject to the reductions in 1108.7. OSSC 1108.7.2 then says a multistory dwelling unit not provided with elevator service is not required to be a Type B unit. Every unit of this pod is two storeys and there is no elevator, so no unit is required to be Type B, so 1106.3 never fires and the building owes zero accessible spaces. Table 350-3's Disabled row (13 ft against the standard 9) therefore never applies, and would have been superseded anyway -- ORS 447.233 and the federal standard put a lone accessible space at van-accessible width, 9 ft plus an 8 ft aisle. Closed as other_building rather than preempted: the requirement is real and reaches buildings with elevator service or with ground-storey units, just not this one. It reopens if the product ever becomes single-storey flats, because OSSC 1108.7.1 keeps the ground storey of a non-elevator building on the Type B hook. Full reasoning, the city-by-city read, and the sources are in docs/HUMAN_TODO.md item 4.
